extra.reason: Resolved: revise. ADR 0001 replaces the category ban with a cost test — every stage and epic declares a standing cost in minutes/dollars per month, over budget for two consecutive retros means deleted or automated. Fleets and inter-agent protocols scoped as fw-oef and fw-wb2. Binding constraint recorded as review capacity, not compute.

ADR 0002 written (docs/adr/0002-operate-is-a-stage.md): Operate becomes the sixth stage between Release and Learn, owning slo.yml, the prober, incident lifecycle, and post-deploy smoke/rollback. Paging, on-call, and dashboards-as-product explicitly out of scope.

ADR 0003 written (docs/adr/0003-autonomy-boundaries.md): unattended agents may branch/commit/gate/PR/comment/reserve; may not merge, tag, release, deploy, touch prod, read secrets, force-push, or rewrite the audit log. Hard token and wall-clock caps; failure leaves the bead open with a comment rather than closing it.

ADR 0004 written (docs/adr/0004-three-layer-agent-architecture.md): beads owns the work graph, blackbird owns coordination (identity, reservations, messages, journal), Claude Code owns execution. bd claims the work, blackbird reserves the files, both required before edit. Nothing blackbird already ships gets rebuilt.

ADR 0006 written: five roles (coordinator/builder/reviewer/operator/retro), only the coordinator stateful. Ceiling derived from review capacity rather than compute — 8 reviewable PRs/day → caps of 6 builder PRs/night, 3 concurrent builders, 2 active repos/night. Caps are numbers so the retro can check them, and they move only on measured merged-without-edits data.

Shipped in flywheel-template c923070: docs/slo.yml declares the contract (url, breach_after, recover_after, latency_budget, availability_target) and healthz.go provides a drop-in Healthz handler serving {status,version,uptime_s} — kept when a project replaces main.go. Version is ldflag-injected so Learn can attribute an incident to a release. Deliberate call: /healthz returns 200 even when degraded, because a 5xx is indistinguishable from the process being down; the body carries the detail. 3 subtests.

Shipped in flywheel-template c923070: tools/watch reads slo.yml, probes /healthz, files exactly one incident-labelled GitHub issue per (target, breach kind), deduped by a fingerprint marker embedded in the issue body rather than by title matching. Stateless — sustain windows are enforced by re-probing, not by remembering across invocations, so it runs identically from a workflow, a cron, or the host. Flat-YAML parsed in ~40 lines rather than taking the template's first dependency (ponytail comment names the ceiling and upgrade path). operate.yml runs it every 30min with a concurrency group so two probers never race. 16 subtests green, vet clean.

Shipped with fw-wma.3 in the same tool: on a healthy probe, watch looks for an open incident matching any breach-kind fingerprint, waits recover_after, re-probes, and closes with a comment stamping the recovery time. A recovery that does not hold leaves the incident open and reports 'flapping'. This is what makes MTTR a measured open→close span rather than a measure of how fast someone clicked Close. Covered by TestRun/recovery_that_holds_closes_the_incident and .../does_not_hold_leaves_it_open.

Shipped in flywheel-template: deploy.sh keeps the outgoing binary as <bin>.prev, polls /healthz after restart for SMOKE_TIMEOUT, and on failure restores the previous build, restarts, and exits 1. Rollback is a local copy rather than a re-download because the network is what you cannot count on mid-rollback. Unset HEALTHZ warns loudly instead of passing silently. VERIFIED locally end-to-end against a deliberately broken build (v1-good -> bad v2 -> smoke fail -> v1-good restored, exit 1) plus happy path and warning path; added ASSET_URL to make that possible without a host. NOT yet verified on the real linux box — that is fw-wma.6, which is blocked on the box existing.

Shipped 13cff31: tools/fleet lease layer. Confirmed first that bd has no lease support — --claim is atomic but has no liveness, and bd stale is day-granularity, far too coarse for a nightly fleet. Lease state lives in the bead's own metadata (beads owns claims, ADR 0004) so it survives the machine that took it. Claim refuses a live lease held by another agent; heartbeat refuses to extend someone else's, which stops a reclaimed agent waking up and editing alongside its replacement; reclaim returns expired leases to open with a note naming who dropped them and warning about stale worktrees, and deliberately leaves unleased in-progress beads alone because those are a human's work. VERIFIED LIVE against the real database: claim -> second agent refused -> heartbeat -> stale agent refused -> status countdown -> expire -> reclaim -> back to open with note. 9 tests.

Shipped 13cff31: fleet/roster.json is the committed capability registry (caps, repos with budgets and paused flags, agents with roles/repos/skills) plus Roster.Match, which joins bead labels of the form lang:* and skill:* against agent skills and repo coverage. Routing verified by tests across 3 repos and 2 languages: a lang:python + skill:jax bead routes to fleet/builder-py, a lang:go bead to fleet/builder-go, and a lang:rust bead is declined with 'no builder in the roster has the required skills' rather than being silently dropped. Roster load rejects non-positive caps citing ADR 0006. Live routing exercised against agentic-flywheel; the router repo declined because its Dolt DB is not hydrated locally (see note on fw-oef.3).

Substrate verified live against the running blackbird daemon and the discipline is now encoded. Verification: an exclusive subtree lease on docs/adr correctly refused a second registered agent's exact-file request inside it with LEASE_CONFLICT — overlap detection works across granularities, which is the property this bead depends on. Acquire returns lease_id + fences + expires_at; release takes lease_id + fences. No new code needed, per ADR 0004. Discipline encoded in .claude/skills/flywheel-next/SKILL.md step 4: acquire the narrowest selectors before the first edit, fail closed (blackbird unreachable is a hard stop), never wait or retry on LEASE_CONFLICT — release, comment on the bead naming the conflict, unclaim, take a different bead. CLAUDE.md carries the short form. Automated two-agent conformance for reservations is fw-wb2.9 (MCP-only API).

Shipped 7c3066e: tools/fleet/conformance_test.go (build tag 'conformance') runs against REAL bd databases in scratch git repos, asserting failure behaviour rather than the happy path — two agents cannot hold one bead; a killed agent's work returns to bd ready with a note naming who dropped it and warning about the stale worktree, and is genuinely re-claimable; a stale agent cannot resurrect its lease alongside its replacement; an unleased in-progress bead (a human's work) is never reclaimed; the kill switch halts a cycle with three builders active; caps hold against a 12-bead queue. 6 conformance tests, ~76s, green. Wired into this repo's new pr.yml as a job that installs bd. It already earned its keep: it exposed non-deterministic plan ordering (equal-priority ties resolved by bd's emission order), fixed by an id tiebreak and guarded by a 20-run reproducibility test. SCOPE: territory/reservation conformance is agent-driven, not in this harness — blackbird's reservation API is MCP-only. Filed as fw-wb2.9.

Shipped in agentic-flywheel PR #3 (validate-v2) + flywheel-template PR #6: .claude/skills/flywheel-review runs correctness, security and simplicity as INDEPENDENT lenses over the same diff — each blind to the others, because a lens that reads another's output will agree with it. Merges and ranks by concrete failure; two lenses on one line is treated as a stronger signal, not a duplicate. Wired into pre-push in both repos, still advisory (|| true), with an explicit instruction to cut to two lenses rather than let the hook get slow enough to be bypassed. Findings recorded via guard.sh finding (fw-l8k.2).

Shipped: guard.sh gained a 'finding' subcommand appending to .flywheel/review.jsonl with ts, commit, branch, repo, lens, file, line, severity, claim and disposition. Verified with quote/tab escaping intact. The skill mandates recording REJECTED findings too — a ledger of only the good calls cannot produce a false-positive rate, and that number is what decides whether the panel earns its cost. Escape-rate correlation (findings vs defects later found by CI or Operate) is the remaining half and belongs with fw-e7e.1's next iteration.

Shipped in flywheel-template PR #6 (green): .goreleaser.yaml gains SBOM per archive, keyless cosign signing via the Actions OIDC token (id-token: write added to release.yml; no key to store, rotate or leak), and the cosign verify-blob command documented inline. Also adds the -X main.Version ldflag, which is what lets Operate attribute an incident to a release via /healthz. All configuration, no code. NOT yet exercised end to end — signing and SBOM only run on a tagged release, so the next tag is the real test.

Shipped in flywheel-template PR #6 (security job PASSED on first run): gitleaks blocks with fetch-depth 0 so it scans history not just the tip — a committed secret is already leaked and failing loudly is the only useful response. govulncheck is advisory and emits a ::warning:: for triage into a bead, because a gate that cries wolf gets bypassed and a bypassed gate is worse than none. Complements the pre-push security lens: the lens reasons about the code, this checks what is verifiably true.

Partially shipped in flywheel-template PR #6: -race is now on by default in the CI unit job for both flywheel-template and agentic-flywheel. Justification recorded inline — CI caught a race the local suite never hit, which is the entire argument for running it there. NOT DONE: fuzz seed corpus and hypothesis property tests; the template's placeholder main.go has no parser surface to fuzz, so that lands with the first real parser (filed as follow-up in the epic body rather than left implied).

Shipped in flywheel-template PR #7: tools/dora/agent.go adds first-pass gate rate, rework (commits after PR open), review round-trips, and autonomous share (bead/* PRs merged with nothing pushed after). All from the GitHub API alone, so they BACKFILL across full history — trend line on day one rather than in a month. Agent metrics are additive and non-fatal; the dashboard renders the panel only when present so old snapshots still display. Cost per PR deliberately excluded: it needs the audit log, not the API, and a number the repo cannot verify has no business on a public dashboard. LIVE BACKFILL: router 13/13 first-pass green (100%), brax 24/25 (96%), median 0 rework in both. DESIGN FLAW CAUGHT BY THE LIVE RUN: the obvious rework metric anchors to the first GitHub review event, which reads zero forever here because review is local (ADR 0002); re-anchored to PR open. The fixture was perfectly happy — only the real repos exposed it.

Shipped in PR #4: roster paths are relative to a workspace root (workspace_root key, then $FLYWHEEL_WORKSPACE, then ~/Workspace) with ~ and $HOME expansion; absolute paths still honoured so an unusual layout stays expressible. The committed roster no longer contains any /home/... path, and TestCommittedRosterHasNoHostPaths asserts that it never does again. Verified: fleet allocate still resolves all repos from the portable roster.

Shipped in PR #4: docs/fleet.html joins every repo's committed dora.json into one page — delivery table (releases, per-week, lead time, CFR, MTTR) and agent table (first-pass gate, rework, round-trips, autonomous share) side by side. No backend; adding a repo is one line. A repo whose snapshot is missing or predates Learn v2 renders as 'no snapshot yet' rather than being omitted, because silence would read as 'nothing to show'. NOT YET LINKED from jamesponwith.github.io — that repo is not cloned here, so publishing the page to the pages site is a remaining step.

Shipped in PR #4: 'fleet bypasses' detects commits that reached main without passing the Validate gate, groups by kind, and reports anything over the budget of 2 (the number SPEC.md itself names) as a gate that should be deleted or automated.

THE CALIBRATION WAS THE WORK. Three rounds against real history:
  1. 30+ reported, including commits that plainly went through PRs — squash merges leave no merge commit, so every squash-merged PR looked like a direct push.
  2. Still counting the Learn workflow's own snapshot commits and every 'bd: close ...' bookkeeping commit.
  3. Excludes squash-merge subjects (…(#N)), bot authors, and the same bookkeeping patterns .goreleaser.yaml already excludes from the changelog — the project had already decided those are not changes, so the detector should not disagree with the changelog.
Each false-positive class has a regression test.

Live result: flywheel-template 1 (its bootstrap commit, under budget), llm-resiliency-router 4, agentic-flywheel 15 — mostly today's direct pushes to main. The tool correctly flags this repo, which is the point. NOT DONE: the auto-filed bead proposing a gate's own deletion; currently it reports and a human acts.

Shipped in PR #5: .claude/skills/flywheel-plan turns a named SPEC.md section into a proposed bd --graph plan — epic, one-session children, verifiable acceptance criteria, and only genuinely-blocking dependency edges (an over-constrained graph looks tidy and starves the queue). Always dry-runs; the human edits the plan rather than the beads afterwards, and the skill states explicitly that halving a proposed plan is a normal outcome. Marks human-decision beads as type=decision + human-only so the coordinator never hands them to a builder. NOT YET RUN against a real spec section — the dogfood benchmark (reproduce this repo's own Chapter 2 epics) is the acceptance test and has not been executed.

Shipped in PR #5: tools/flywheel/bead-lint.sh checks the branch name (bead/<id>) or commit subjects for a real bead id and confirms it exists via bd show. Wired as an 'intent' job in agentic-flywheel's pr.yml. Advisory by default with --strict to block, per ADR 0001's rule that a gate goes blocking only once its noise level is known. Verified on both a real bead branch (bead/fw-oef.8 -> 'bead: fw-oef.8') and a non-bead branch (warns, exits 0). NOT DONE: the merge-side check that every closed bead has a close reason.

Shipped in PR #5 as ADR 0008 + CLAUDE.md: anything expected to exceed one session gets a design note in the bead's --design field first — key types, public signatures, boundaries only, no prose. Rationale recorded: reviewing four signatures takes a minute, reviewing the four hundred lines that follow takes an hour, and with an agent doing the typing, shape is where a human's judgement is cheapest. Deliberately a convention rather than a gate. The ADR commits to judging it honestly in the retro and deleting it if it proves to be ceremony that never changed an implementation.

Shipped in PR #5: .claude/skills/flywheel-retro reads the dora.json git history (including the agent block), closed beads and their close reasons, .flywheel/review.jsonl, fleet bypasses, incidents, and bd stale — together, which is the thing that never happens otherwise. Judges rather than summarises: what got better and can you tell why, what is over its ADR 0001 budget, and what did the metrics not catch. Proposes candidate beads and stops; creating ten unasked is how a board becomes noise. Carries an honesty clause — if the evidence says the flywheel is not paying for itself, recommend deleting something, and if three consecutive retros produce proposals nobody acts on, propose deleting the skill itself. NOT DONE: the monthly cron that fires it unattended.

Done and verified live. blackbird_agent_register is idempotent per (project_key, agent_name) and returns a registration_token that authenticates subsequent calls and resumes the same identity across restarts — exercised repeatedly this session (fleet/builder-go, fleet/reviewer-security, flywheel/builder). Naming convention <repo-or-fleet>/<role>[-<lens>] is codified in fleet/roster.json (8 agents across 5 roles) and used throughout the audit log, which is what makes the log readable. Token custody: tokens live in the run sandbox/XDG state and never in the repo — enforced rather than hoped, since gitleaks now blocks on committed secrets (fw-l8k.4) and a full-history scan for bbm_ tokens came back clean before the first push.

Shipped in PR #5 as ADR 0007: one blackbird conversation per bead, four message types and no others — handoff (builder->reviewer, ack required), finding (reviewer->builder, ack optional), escalate (any agent->human, ack required), status (no ack). An unacknowledged handoff past its TTL escalates rather than stalling silently. Reasoning recorded for the closed set: open-ended agent chat is a token bonfire with no audit value, and an agent with no defined way to say 'I am stuck' will instead do something confident and wrong. Four types are countable, so escalation rate becomes a measure of how well beads are specified. NOT YET EXERCISED: no build->review->fix cycle has run through the contract end to end.

Shipped in PR #7 (stacked on #4): 'fleet doctor' diagnoses every roster repo against a data-driven Manifest — 17 artifacts across six stages plus agent tooling, each carrying the reason it exists, because a checklist nobody understands gets ignored. Adding a stage artifact is a line, not code. Language-specific entries are skipped rather than reported (a Go release config is not missing from a Python repo), and required artifacts sort first. '-fix' installs from a source template and REFUSES to overwrite — a doctor that clobbers local customisation is worse than the drift it fixes; a test asserts a customised SPEC.md survives. 7 tests. EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN: it found that agentic-flywheel, the repo that defines the Learn stage, had no learn.yml and was not running Learn on itself — fixed in the same PR. Also correctly identified that the router and template both lack the Operate contract and agent tooling. NOT DONE: '-fix' has not been exercised against a real instance, because the artifacts it would copy are still on unmerged template branches (#6, #7 there).

Merged as PR #2. WRITEUP.md now describes six stages, gives Operate its own section (the stage invisible at C1 because tenants owned the telemetry), and replaces the 'Dropped: orchestration, agent fleets, inter-agent protocols' paragraph — which contradicted the shipped code — with the budget-not-ban story plus the review-capacity constraint. Adds a 'What I still can't tell you' section carrying the real backfilled numbers (100% first-pass on the router, 96% on brax, median 0 rework) while explicitly distrusting them: a solo repo has no reviewer to send work back, so 'no rework' partly measures the absence of a second opinion. Token cost and review escape rate named as genuinely unknown. The voice pass (c37430c) preserved throughout. REMAINING: publish it (fw-fsa.5).
